title: add RAG agent tool-calling quickstarts and docs site updates
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Added RAG agent quickstarts, tool-calling examples, and docs site navigation updates. No breaking changes.
description: This PR adds a set of RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) agent quickstarts and tool-calling examples to the docs site and redwood-examples repo. Motivation: provide customers with runnable, opinionated templates that demonstrate combining vector stores, Redwood agents, and external tools (search, calendar, and DB connectors) using our tool-calling API. The work includes new quickstart guides, sample configs, CI examples, and minor docs-site navigation updates so the content is discoverable from the main "Getting started" flow. Checklist: - [x] Add four quickstart examples (python, typescript, curl, and docker) - [x] Add agent templates with standard tool interfaces (search, calendar, sql) - [x] Add sample dataset indexing script and vector-store config - [x] Add docs-site pages and sidebar entries - [x] Update examples to use the stable tool-calling schema and streaming examples - [x] Add basic integration CI to run quickstart smoke tests - [x] Docs copy review and runbook link included Changeset: high-level commit list and small diffs attached below. Caveats: The SQL connector is a demo shim (see README); customers should replace with their own auth and KMS config for production. Related: Linear ENG-4821, prior PRs that started the RAG templates work (see pr-49234 and pr-49111).

notes: This is the first public set of RAG agent quickstarts that demonstrate tool-calling in combination with a vector store. Follow-up work: add Rust example and additional secure SQL connector template (tracked in ENG-4890).
end_user_impact: New docs and quickstarts are additive and should not affect existing APIs. The examples are gated behind example repos and do not modify runtime behavior.
qa_instructions: Run .github/workflows/rag-quickstart-smoke.yml locally (or via GH actions) to ensure quickstarts start, index the sample dataset, and execute one agent run that calls the search tool and streams a response.
